newsitem.title: CANADA: Hearing date for Thai banker moved to Sept. 25.
newsitem.headline: Hearing date for Thai banker moved to Sept. 25.

text.p: A Canadian court on Wednesday postponed a decision on when it would start extradition proceedings against a former Thai bank official arrested in Canada on fraud charges.

The date was to have been set on Wednesday, but attorneys for Rakesh Saxena, a former treasury adviser for the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce, won a two-week postponement to Sept. 25. The court did not explain the reason for the delay.

Saxena, 45, an Indian national and resident of Thailand, was arrested on fraud charges in early July by Canadian and Thai police for allegedly colluding with a group of other senior bank executives in embezzling $63.3 million.
He was granted bail by a British Columbia supreme court judge following his arrest on condition that he post C$1.25 million (US $909,000) and surrender his passport.

Saxena, who was an independent treasury adviser to the bank, denied all charges. At least four bank employees, including its president, have appeared before the courts in Thailand and were released on bail.

The Thai government took control of the bank in May after it faced a heavy public run on its deposits. The country's central bank has said that Bangkok Bank of Commerce has more than $3 billion of bad, risky and non-performing loans.
